report:
Fresh source assessment of crates.sage_test_harness.compile_tests.coordinates using the current start inputs and captured review_scope rule. I inspected the current claim, all three ordinary implementation associations and their whole-file context, and all three complete ordinary associated tests. No TODO/N/A evidence is present.

The claim requires (1) inspecting the evaluated source expression, including indoc! results; (2) no additional dedenting; (3) physical line coordinates including annotation lines; (4) rejection of actual tabs; and (5) type selection independent of Unicode width and horizontal alignment. In compile/mod.rs the macro accepts source as an expression and passes its value to CompileTest::source. source and files copy the resulting string; validate_files validates paths and clones source without transformation; prepare parses and writes that same source. There is no trimming or independent dedenting. The indoc! case is covered by the general expression evaluation mechanism, with no special textual macro interpretation.

annotations.rs parses the actual source, rejects source.contains('\t') before parsing, and obtains comment row/byte-column positions from tree-sitter. Splitting on newline preserves annotation and blank lines. It uses columns only to distinguish inline from annotation-only comments, and stores a one-based target line. Annotation-only lines are skipped as candidate targets but never removed from coordinate accounting. Marker has no column field that could constrain expression selection.

observe.rs builds target pairs of file and line and selects rows solely by those fields. walk_expr computes line by counting newline bytes preceding the absolute source span; unmatched-source rows use the same calculation. Unicode scalar/display widths and indentation do not participate. The relevant coordinate-preservation, marker-location, and selection helpers are in the already captured associated files; no further source helper is needed to establish these coordinate decisions. Type inference and expression enumeration are upstream inputs to these decisions, not alternate coordinate selectors.

Complete test coverage: inline_stacked_and_blank_lines_use_one_rule explicitly asserts [2, 2, 2, 6] for inline/stacked markers, blank lines and an ordinary comment after annotation lines, and requires a tabs error for a source containing an actual tab. It catches removal of annotation lines from coordinates and loss of tab rejection. evaluated_source_retains_blank_lines_indentation_and_unicode passes an intentionally leading-blank-line, indented source with café, then asserts physical line 2 and exact indentation in rendered lines 2 and 3, including the annotation text. Those assertions would fail for trimming/dedenting or renumbering. unicode_and_indentation_do_not_change_line_type_selection supplies an indented Unicode function with a trailing marker horizontally beyond its expressions; the exact inline snapshot requires both the true literal and enclosing block, each bool. This would reject column-aligned selection or selection corrupted by multibyte width. Assertions are visible in the test bodies and collectively cover the complete claim.

I found no source defect or missing test requirement and request no edits. This refresh is source inspection only: I executed review start/read/record commands, not behavior tests or a build. The coordinator owns current suite execution; earlier test outcomes are not claimed as fresh evidence. No source or test changes were made.
